title: Best Baby Bottles UK
short: Seven baby bottles compared on leak-proofing, durability, cleaning, sterilising and how well they suit newborns, breastfed babies and colic.
intro: Bottle use is very personal: what suits one baby won't suit another. This guide is based on Mumsnet's tested roundup (updated March 2026), where a mum-of-two tester spent several weeks washing, filling and sterilising each bottle, filled them with boiling water to time how long they could be held and check for squirting from the teat, dropped them on a hard floor, and scrubbed them hard to see whether markings came off. Bottles were scored on purchase and assembly, safety and stability, day-to-day use, cleanliness, looks and value, and Mumsnet also drew on parent recommendations. Prices shown are RRPs quoted by Mumsnet. If your baby is struggling to feed, speak to your midwife, health visitor or a feeding specialist.

products.name: Easy Start Anti-Colic Bottles
products.best_for: Families who want self-sterilising bottles that suit newborns and colicky babies
products.key_spec: 260ml (also 160ml), self-sterilising in the microwave, vented base, dishwasher-safe, BPA- and BPS-free
products.summary: Mumsnet's Best Buy. Its tester found a solid bottle that handled all the tests brilliantly. It self-sterilises (add water and microwave for about three minutes), so no separate steriliser is needed, which suits travelling or small kitchens, and its vented, removable base helps a baby swallow less air. It's one of the most inexpensive on the market. It can leak if the top or base isn't screwed on properly, and the extra parts make assembly longer.

specs.Teats: Sizes 1 to 3, then X (faster flow) and non-spill
specs.Made from: BPA- and BPS-free plastic and silicone

cons: Can leak if the top or bottom isn't screwed on properly
Extra parts make for longer assembly

products.name: Feeding Bottles with NaturalWave Teats
products.best_for: Breastfed babies and parents wanting paced bottle feeding
products.key_spec: 160ml and 260ml, NaturalWave silicone teat, vented, three-part design, dishwasher-safe
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester found it sturdily made, calling it 'quite frankly, indestructible': it showed no damage after scrubbing or being dropped, and didn't drip at all. Its big selling point is the soft NaturalWave teat, designed to encourage a baby's natural tongue movement, which suits newborns and breastfed babies and paced feeding. Mumsnet notes Lansinoh bottles are the ones most often recommended on its forums for babies used to the breast. It can discolour in a dishwasher with tomato sauce.

specs.Made from: BPA- and BPS-free plastic and silicone

pros: Three-part design is easy to assemble and clean
Vented teat prevents baby swallowing air
cons: Will discolour in a dishwasher with tomato sauce

products.name: First Choice+ Baby Bottles
products.key_spec: 150ml and 300ml, orthodontic-shaped teat, temperature indicator, anti-colic valve
products.summary: Tried and tested by Mumsnet: cute, reasonably priced and often used in hospitals, with an orthodontically-shaped teat that many parents find easier for breastfed babies to latch onto. The easy-flow teat has its hole on the side, which means more accidental leaks and splashes than other bottles, though sealing discs are provided for transit. Volume markings are grey and hard to read in dim light, and the narrow neck needs a brush, which isn't included.

specs.Made from: BPA- and BPS-free plastic and silicone

pros: Mumsnetters say they're great for combination feeding
cons: Grey volume marks are hard to see

products.name: Options+ Anti-Colic Bottles
products.best_for: Babies with colic, wind or reflux
products.key_spec: 150ml and 270ml, internal vent system, vacuum-free silicone teat, removable vent
products.summary: Mumsnet says many parents with colicky babies swear by these, and the internal vent and vacuum-free teat are designed to reduce wind, reflux and burping. The vent can be removed as colic risk falls with age, so the bottle 'grows' with your baby. They are dishwasher-safe but a little fiddly to dismantle, clean and reassemble.
pros: Internal vent system designed to decrease reflux, burping and wind
Silicone teats provide consistent, vacuum-free flow
Vent system can be removed when not needed

products.name: Natural Response Baby Bottle
products.best_for: A reliable, basic mid-priced bottle with an anti-colic valve
products.key_spec: 125ml, 260ml and 330ml, anti-colic valve, teat mimics breastmilk flow, leak-proof
products.summary: Mumsnet found a good-quality, leak-proof bottle with a valved teat that mimics breastmilk flow and helps keep air away from the baby's tummy. Many Mumsnet users like it as a mid-range option, though there isn't much to set it apart from the crowd, and some Mumsnetters prefer Dr Brown's for colicky babies.
pros: Anti-colic valve keeps air away from baby's tummy
Teat designed to mimic breastfeeding let-down
cons: No real standout features from other bottles
products.search: Philips Avent Natural Response baby bottle

products.name: Natural Start Anti-Colic Baby Bottle
products.best_for: Stocking up on bottles to see which one your baby takes to
products.key_spec: 150ml, 260ml and 340ml, soft silicone valved teat, dishwasher-safe
products.summary: Mumsnet found pretty basic but good-quality bottles, with a soft silicone teat that flexes and stretches like a real nipple and an ergonomic shape that supports a good latch. A multi-pack is a good way to try them. Some reviewers reported leaking during feeds, so make sure the lid is fastened properly, and the lid leaves a lip inside that can trap the last of the milk.
pros: Soft silicone teat flexes and stretches like a real nipple
cons: The lid leaves a lip inside that can trap the last of the milk
products.search: Tommee Tippee Natural Start anti-colic baby bottle

products.name: Baby Bottle
products.best_for: Parents who want an easy-clean, colourful bottle for formula on the go
products.key_spec: 180ml, 260ml and 330ml, extra-wide neck, formula container and mixer net, dishwasher- and steriliser-safe
products.summary: Mumsnet found a strikingly designed, tough BPA-free bottle with an extra-wide neck for easy cleaning and filling, plus a formula container and mixer net. The teat has an anti-colic air valve. It isn't compatible with breast pumps, and in the white model tested the white measurements were hard to see when it was full of milk.

specs.Teats: Small, medium, large and extra large
specs.Made from: BPA- and BPS-free plastic and silicone

pros: Comes with a container and mixer net for formula
cons: Less support and compatibility than other bottles, not compatible with breast pumps
White markings on the white model are hard to see with milk in

guide.q: What size bottle should I buy for a newborn?
guide.a: Mumsnet suggests buying the next size up from the smallest, because your baby will be drinking more milk before you know it. What matters most is the teat flow rate: use the age guide on teats only as a rough guide.

guide.q: How do I know when to move up a teat size?
guide.a: Mumsnet says if your baby takes longer than 20 minutes to finish a feed, falls asleep regularly while feeding or tugs at the teat, it may be a sign they're ready for the next size up. Slow flow stops small babies guzzling and choking, while faster flow spares bigger babies from working too hard.

guide.q: Which bottle is best for a breastfed baby or for colic?
guide.a: Mumsnet's forums most often recommend Lansinoh for babies used to the breast, and Dr Brown's for colic. It is a matter of trial and error, though, since every baby is different. If feeding problems continue, ask your midwife, health visitor or a feeding specialist.

Not with a self-sterilising bottle like the MAM Easy Start, where you add water to the base and microwave for about three minutes. Other bottles here are dishwasher-safe and can go in a separate steriliser, so check the manufacturer's instructions for sterilising.
